SOBHA Limited's flagship projects include SOBHA Altus in Delhi NCR, SOBHA Neopolis and SOBHA Ayana in Bangalore, and SOBHA Elysia in GIFT City. The company's portfolio covers residential projects like apartments, villas, row houses, townships, and plotted developments, as well as commercial real estate projects. SOBHA also offers interior design and manufacturing services, including glazing and metal works, and concrete products manufacturing.

SOBHA currently operates in Bangalore, Delhi NCR, Coimbatore, Pune, Kochi, Kozhikode, Trivandrum, Thrissur, Chennai, Hyderabad, and GIFT City Gujarat – with expansion plans in other key markets.

Sobha Limited differentiates itself through a precision-led model focused on brand trust and quality, positioning itself as a premium developer, particularly in markets like Bangalore. It employs a backward-integrated operating model that covers design, construction, glazing, metalwork, interiors, and concrete products, which is a structural differentiator from developers relying on subcontractors. Sobha also emphasizes execution and execution-based profits, rarely facing large-scale delivery credibility issues compared to peers. Additionally, it has a net cash position, limits on debt, and a preference for self-funded growth, providing protection against real estate cycles and flexibility to acquire land opportunistically.

From humble beginnings in Kerala, India, Mr. PNC Menon built a reputation for quality, detail, and trustworthiness, earning him major construction commissions in the Gulf region. This paved the way for venturing into real estate development in Dubai, UAE. Striving to control quality and schedule, his firm, Sobha Middle East, self-performs a wide range of tasks – an unusual set of choices in the global real estate and construction industry. In mid-2018, the 70 year old entrepreneur and his team [...] Meanwhile, sitting in Bangalore, PNC Menon’s son Ravi Menon, Chairman of publicly listed Sobha India, is facing a typical in-house versus outsource decision. Sobha India had pioneered the backward integration strategy prior to Dubai. Ravi Menon and his team are deciding on the structural system for Sobha Bellahalli complex of 5,000 apartments in Bangalore. Should they deploy a cast in place structural frame or invest in a precast concrete manufacturing plant on site? Additionally, should they [...] and his team are contemplating their longer term strategy, particularly regarding land acquisition, construction strategy, and financing. Is the backward integration model replicable and sustainable?
